TITLE:  Multi-Step Forecasting with Adaptive Attention 
PROPOSAL: We develop an online forecasting method, dubbed OAA-TS (Online Attention Adaptation for Time Series), that leverages an attention mechanism to selectively focus on the most relevant information for multi-step forecasting. At each time step, OAA-TS automatically updates its attention weights to adjust to evolving patterns in the data, including concept drift, using a small batch of recent samples. This dynamic attention mechanism adaptively allocates more weights to the recently updated parameters, ensuring that the model stays attuned to the latest patterns and minimizes the impact of delayed and noisy feedback from multi-step forecasts.

PROPOSAL: We introduce a new mechanism for stabilizing online time series forecasters by maintaining a complementary slow-stream update, dubbed SSW (Slow Stream Weights), in parallel to the fast stream updated with gradients from recent samples. This allows the fast stream to adapt quickly to changing patterns while maintaining overall stability and ensuring long-term consistency. The key is to adaptively adjust the fraction of weights updated by SSW at each step based on a learned stability metric, which balances short-term adaptability and long-term reliability.
